dossier.scp_unleashed.244.title: Ice Fog Jars
dossier.scp_unleashed.244.caption: SCP-244-A to C at intake, lids sealed. Frost formed on the tag overnight.

page.title: Special Containment Procedures:
text: The three vessels of SCP-244 are to be stored upright with their lids in place, on separate shelves of a dry storage room. Each is checked weekly for frost along the lid seam.
A lid may be lifted only during approved testing, in a sealed chamber whose doors can be shut from outside. **No vessel is to be opened in a room that someone must cross to leave.**
Personnel attending a test wear cold weather gear and keep their exposure as brief as possible.

page.title: Description:
text: SCP-244 is a set of three lidded ceramic vessels of uncertain age: a slender celadon amphora (SCP-244-A), a squat bone white urn painted with faded blue flowers (SCP-244-B) and a pale ginger jar with indigo blossoms (SCP-244-C). All three are cold to the touch.

When a lid is lifted, a dense grey fog pours from the vessel's mouth. Within seconds it fills the room the vessel stands in, flowing through open doorways and along corridors but not past shut doors or solid walls. It never travels far from its source.

The fog is intensely cold. Subjects within it report numbness, then stiffness, then pain, and their injuries resemble severe frostbite. Effects worsen the longer a subject remains and the nearer they stand to the open vessel. Standing water within the fog freezes, and frost may settle on the floor.
When the lid is replaced the flow stops at once, but the fog lingers for some time before it thins away. Until it has cleared, the vessel cannot be lifted from where it stands.

page.title: Addendum 244-1: Test Log
text: Test 244-03: SCP-244-B was opened in an empty chamber. The chamber was filled to the ceiling within seconds and every thermometer inside failed.
Test 244-06: the chamber door was left open. The fog followed the corridor beyond for some distance, then stopped as if it had reached a wall.
Test 244-09: a subject in a heavy hide coat remained in the fog for noticeably longer than an unprotected subject. %rFurther results withheld.%r
Test 244-11: a pail of water left in the chamber was found frozen solid.

page.title: Addendum 244-2: Provenance
page.text: SCP-244 was found in a long sealed storeroom, packed together in one straw lined crate. It was delivered to a reader of this file by the individual in Foundation dress described in the files of other objects. See field notes.

jei.scp_unleashed.info.scp244_vase.1: SCP-244 is a set of three old lidded ceramic vessels: a slender amphora, a squat urn and a ginger jar. Each one is cold to the touch.
jei.scp_unleashed.info.scp244_vase.2: Lifting a lid releases a dense, freezing grey fog. It pours over the rim and fills the room the vessel stands in, flowing through open doorways but not past solid walls or shut doors.
jei.scp_unleashed.info.scp244_vase.3: Anything caught in the fog begins to freeze, faster the longer it stays and the closer it stands to the open vessel. Standing water in the fog ices over.
jei.scp_unleashed.info.scp244_vase.4: Putting the lid back stops the flow, but the fog lingers for a while before it thins away, and the vessel stays frozen to the floor until it does. The set cannot be crafted; a stranger in Foundation dress delivers it. Each vessel fits in a storage container.
archive.scp_unleashed.notes.scp244.0: A courier hands over all three jars together.
